title: Lisandro Martinez to miss Manchester United’s Chelsea trip through suspension – Michael Carrick
content:
Lisandro Martinez will miss Manchester United’s trip to Chelsea on Saturday through suspension after his red card for a hair pull on Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Michael Carrick has said.

The 28-year-old Argentina international was dismissed in Monday’s defeat at home to Leeds United after VAR John Brooks called referee Paul Tierney to the screen for the incident, which United appealed on the grounds Martinez did not pull with force and was challenging for the ball.

Referees told clubs at the start of the season hair pulling would be seen as violent conduct and Michael Carrick confirmed during Friday’s press conference United had to “accept” the verdict and “move on”.

Should the defender miss three games, as is typical for offences deemed to be ‘violent conduct’, Martinez would also miss league games against Brentford and Liverpool, meaning he would next be available for the game at Sunderland on May 9.

Martinez’s absence is compounded by Harry Maguire’s suspension after his sending off against Bournemouth. He had a misconduct charge held up against him the red card on March 20. Both the red card and follow-up misconduct charge resulted in two one-match suspensions, the first of which was served against Leeds on Monday.

“We didn’t agree with it, it’s obvious how I felt after the game, and I still feel that way now,” United head coach Michael Carrick said on Friday. “I don’t want to go into it now, it is what it is. We have to accept it and move on.”

On Monday, Carrick described the red card as a “shocking decision”.

Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven are the only recognised centre-backs in United’s senior squad, with Matthijs de Ligt still unavailable through a long-term absence. Manuel Ugarte, a midfielder by trade, played in defence following Martinez’s red card against Leeds.

Kobbie Mainoo, who missed Monday’s match through injury, is in contention to feature against Chelsea. “There is a decision to be made,” said Carrick.

Patrick Dorgu, who has been out through injury since January, remains unavailable.
